transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Start time: 14:23 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (NexGen Product), Tom Weller (NexGen ML Eng), Priya Singh (NexGen Security)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): okay everyone thanks for jumping on, quick agenda — model gating rules, fallback / escape hatch design, next steps for the pilot
00:12 Tom Weller (Customer): yeah thanks Samira, we ran the night batch with the latest prompt set and saw some p99 spikes when sequences hit ~6k tokens
00:25 Diego (Redwood SE): mhm, that's consistent with what we saw on our side on the prod-ish workload, curious — was KV cache enabled for that job?
00:33 Tom: it was partially enabled, but we only warmed the prefix cache for common queries, long tails were cold
00:40 Aisha: our main success criteria are p95 < 300ms for typical 512 token responses and p95 < 700ms for longer 2-4k responses, anything above that and the UX degrades
00:52 Speaker 2 (Samira): noted. So two levers we discussed — automatic gating by latency and by quality regressions. We should be explicit about thresholds and about what "escape" looks like
01:10 Priya (Security): and from security side, we need to ensure any automatic fallback doesn't route to third-party models without audit logs and KMS protections
01:22 Diego: absolutely; fallback options we propose: 1) quantized version of same model (lower perf but same architecture), 2) smaller variant from our catalog pinned to customer, 3) cached/templated response for certain classes
01:38 Tom: are there measurable quality drop numbers between full FP16 and 4-bit quant that we can expect? we can't accept >3% drop in F1 on our intent classifier
01:48 Diego: ballpark — for our seq2seq style generation, structured outputs, 4-bit tends to add noise in edge cases; for many prompts it's within 1-2% on our eval set, but we need your prompt set to verify
02:02 Samira: so propose gating rules: primary gate = p95 latency; secondary gate = quality regression on rolling prompt set (we'll run evals every 2 hours during canary)
02:16 Aisha: what about circuit breakers — immediate fallback if p99 > 1.5s for three consecutive 1-minute windows?
02:25 Diego: yes, that's a good circuit breaker. Also soft gate: start automated traffic shift to the fallback at 5% increments when p95 breaches threshold but not p99
02:36 Tom: how do we avoid cascading failures — e.g., if smaller model also hits latency under load
02:44 Diego: good point — we recommend multi-factor gating: before shifting more traffic we verify target variant meets throughput in a short synthetic warm up (we'll run a micro-ramp for 2 minutes)
02:57 Priya: auditability — can we ensure every fallback action is logged with reason codes and an irreversible record in the customer's audit log? we need retention for 1 year
03:10 Samira: yes, Redwood will emit a fallback event with reason, metrics snapshot, and model_version ids; we'll surface in Console and push to your SIEM via webhook
03:21 Aisha: ok, let's get specific on thresholds. Tom — what's acceptable p95 for 2-4k tokens again?
03:29 Tom: we want p95 < 700ms ideally, hard limit 1.2s
03:36 Diego: noted: initial p95 gates we'll set to 300ms for 512 tokens, 700ms for 2-4k; circuit breaker p99 at 1.5s across ANY seq len
03:49 Speaker 1 (Samira): another consideration — version pinning strategy: we can pin by model_version or by model_family+quant profile
04:02 Diego: yes, pinning by family+profile gives flexibility to switch kernels/compilations without changing the API, but it can mask model weight changes, so for strict reproducibility pin model_version
04:17 Tom: for the pilot we want reproducibility for evaluation, so let's pin model_version for initial 2 weeks, then switch to family+profile for gradual ops
04:27 Aisha: that sounds reasonable
04:33 Priya: also need SSO and RBAC to ensure only ops can trigger manual rollbacks
04:39 Samira: we will add RBAC controls into the canary runbook, only two designated owners to approve manual rollbacks
04:48 Diego: on the operational playbook — we'll deliver two playbooks: auto-fallback playbook and manual rollback runbook; both include metrics, steps, rollback commands and contacts
05:02 Tom: can Redwood do shadow routing so we can measure quality of fallback candidates without user impact?
05:09 Diego: yes, shadowing is supported — we'll run a shadow for the quantized variant and smaller model in parallel for 24 hours before any traffic shift
05:18 Aisha: excellent. For test coverage, we'll pass 1k synthetic prompts that exercise edge intents
05:25 Tom: note — some prompts trigger long LL sequences with heavy memory usage, might need larger KV cache sizing to avoid evicts
05:34 Diego: we'll size cache based on working set you send, but escaping to smaller models reduces memory pressure as well
05:40 Samira: let's document an escape hierarchy: 1) KV/prefix cache warming and micro-batch tuning, 2) switch to quantized variant, 3) shift partial traffic to smaller model, 4) serve cached templates for known intents, 5) degrade to reduced functionality mode (e.g., brief generic fallback)
06:03 Priya: for number 4 (cached templates) we need to ensure PII is not stored; accept only hash keys and template ids
06:12 Diego: agreed — Redwood supports encryption-at-rest and KMS-managed keys; we'll ensure template storage uses customer KMS
06:21 Tom: what's the timeline for the canary? how long do we run each step
06:27 Samira: propose: 48 hours of monitored 5% canary with auto-eval every 2 hours, if stable move to 20% for 24h, then 50% for 24h, then full
06:39 Aisha: and we want the option to abort within 10 minutes
06:44 Diego: our abort action can cut traffic instantly and replay to fallback variant
06:49 Speaker 3 (Customer - Tom): minor thing — do we have cost estimates for the different fallbacks? quantized vs smaller model vs caching
06:57 Samira: we'll provide a delta matrix; rough guidance: quantized reduces token cost ~30-40%, smaller model reduces cost 50-70% depending on family, but watch for quality drop
07:10 Priya: on compliance — please send SOC2 cert plus any pen-test report if available
07:17 Samira: will send SOC2 & KMS integration docs after this call
07:21 Diego: technical task: we need to run a latency sweep. I'll set up a job that runs your representative prompt set at 512/2048/8192 tokens and collect p50/p95/p99 and tail latencies
07:34 Tom: I'll drop the prompt set and 1000 anonymized examples into the shared drive by tomorrow
07:39 Aisha: is there anything we should change in the API layer to support canary toggles?
07:44 Diego: no code changes required — routing policy in Console handles canaries and pins, but we will provide a template config you can review
07:53 Samira: ok recap — Diego to run latency sweep and shadow runs; Tom to provide prompts; Samira to send pricing and security docs; next sync Friday same time to review results
08:06 Speaker 1 (Samira): any other Qs?
08:09 Tom: one last question — if a fallback triggers, will user requests see different model ids in telemetry? we need end-to-end traceability
08:18 Diego: yes, each request keeps model_version metadata, fallback events annotate requests, and traces link to fallback reason codes
08:29 Priya: perfect. I'll also want a runbook entry about how to prove no unpermitted external routing occurred
08:36 Samira: we'll include that in the manual rollback runbook
08:40 Aisha: thanks everyone
08:42 Samira: thanks team, we'll follow up with the artifacts — meeting adjourned

End transcript (approx 54 min). Some portions auto-transcribed; names occasionally mismatched. Notes: mention of exact numbers and dates in next_steps/action_items above.
